title: Usage Signal Runbook: automated triage + mitigation for cost/latency anomalies
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Deliver a pragmatic, automatable runbook and triage playbook for the console backend usage analytics pipeline that covers detection, classification, and automated mitigations for anomalies in usage/cost/latency metrics. This ticket includes: (1) canonical list of signals and dimensionality for detection, (2) detection algorithms and thresholds per signal, (3) automated classification rules that map alerts to likely root causes, (4) immediate mitigation playbook actions that can be executed automatically or by on-call, and (5) integration points (Grafana dashboards, Dataflow/Beam jobs, BigQuery queries, PagerDuty, Slack, Console Incident View). The goal is to reduce mean time to detection (MTTD) and mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for incidents where customer bill or latency spikes exceed normal bounds or threaten SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook covering at least: cost-per-minute, p95/p99 latency by route/model, token ingestion rate, queued requests, batch size distribution, and KV cache hit rate
Automated detectors deployed to staging that produce synthetic alerts for 3 fault modes: sudden traffic surge, regression in batching/kv-cache, and a model quantization misconfiguration
Alert -> classification mapping that correctly tags >=80% of synthetic incidents with root_cause labels: traffic_spike, batching_regression, cache_eviction, pricing_leak, hardware_degradation
Playbook steps include exact queries/commands, 1-click mitigation links (scale up pool, force-fallback to cheaper model, enable token rate-cap), and validated PagerDuty escalation mapping
Metrics emitted to console: alert_type, confidence_score, automated_action_taken, action_result (success/failure)
notes_and_progress: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Observability, Platform, and Infra teams. Agreed to reuse existing Dataflow jobs for metric rollups. Action: Priya to prototype classification rules using historical incidents dataset (s3://redwood-incidents/usage).

2026-03-04: Prototype detector implemented using rolling-median + MAD on ingestion rate and p95 latency. Early tests flagged known post-deploy regressions from Jan-Feb. Noted high false positives on weekends due to weekly cadence. Action: add day-of-week seasonal adjustment.

2026-03-06: Design review with PM (Ariella Park) and Observability (Mateo Ruiz). Feedback: surface per-customer economic impact estimate in the alert (estimated $/hour at current run-rate). Added to acceptance criteria. Follow-up: add BigQuery UDF to compute cost projection.

2026-03-08: Implemented classification heuristics: (1) traffic_spike if ingestion_rate increases >5x baseline and p95 remains stable, (2) batching_regression if batch_size median drops >30% and per-token cost increases, (3) cache_eviction if KV cache hit rate drops >20% and latency tails spike. Benchmarked against 12 historical incidents: classification precision 0.78, recall 0.72. Need to tune confidence thresholds to hit 0.8 precision target.

2026-03-10: Built synthetic incident harness (integration test) that can inject three fault modes into staging pipeline. Harness resides in github.com/redwood-inference/obs-tests/tree/main/usage-anomaly. Added test cases to CI to ensure detectors alert in <2 minutes for injected faults.

2026-03-11: Safety review: automated mitigations are limited to non-destructive actions by default (scale-up, temporary rate-cap, switch to fallback model). Any action that could affect customer data path requires manual approval in Slack + PagerDuty SD escalation. Documented escalation thresholds and manual overrides.
2026-03-12: Preparing runbook pages and Grafana dashboard links. Next: ship detectors to canary, run 72h observation window, measure alert noise and action success rate.
runbook_steps: Detection: alert triggers when metric deviates from seasonal-adjusted rolling median by >5 MAD (or EWMA drift >3 sigma for latency tails)
Enrichment: attach dimensions route, model, region, customer_tier, tokens_last_5m, batch_median_5m, kv_cache_hit_5m; compute estimated_econ_impact = tokens_last_5m * avg_cost_per_token
Classification: apply heuristic rules (traffic_spike, batching_regression, cache_eviction, pricing_leak, infra_cpu_hotspot). If none match, tag as unknown and route to SRE ops queue

Automated mitigation (low-risk): 1) scale dedicated GPU pool +30% for route/model; 2) enable fallback-model policy for affected customers; 3) apply per-customer token rate-cap with 10% ramp-down. These actions are executed by orchestrator with automatic rollback if error rate increases

Manual mitigation (high-risk or unknown): follow Slack path: #inc-ops -> @oncall escalation -> run specific BigQuery diagnostics, revert recent config changes, or trigger container restart. Provide exact commands in documentation
Post-incident: record incident in retros (Confluence link), attach detector logs, adjust detection thresholds or classification rules, and schedule follow-up engineering tasks
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: high false positive rate during seasonal events (product launches, marketing campaigns). Mitigation: incorporate campaign calendar and run sampling suppression with higher thresholds for flagged windows.

Risk: automated mitigations may hide underlying regressions. Mitigation: every automated action emits a mandatory ticket and kicks off a follow-up regression test within 24h; also set a max cumulative automation time per customer per 7d.
Risk: cost estimation inaccuracies leading to poor prioritization. Mitigation: include 95% CI in cost projection, and surface both estimated and observed cost impact after mitigation
